title: Phrasal Verbs: Off & Out
completion_message: ¡Formidable! Dominar los Phrasal Verbs con 'off' y 'out' te da una precisión absoluta en el entorno laboral. 'Phase out' un producto antiguo o 'Roll out' uno nuevo son frases que escucharás a diario en las altas esferas corporativas.

parts.visual:
Los Phrasal Verbs con 'Off' suelen indicar separación, cancelación o finalización: 

1. Call off (Cancelar): 
Ej: We had to CALL OFF the meeting due to the strike. 

2. Write off (Dar por perdido / Cancelar una deuda): 
Ej: The bank will WRITE OFF the bad loan. 

3. Put off (Posponer): 
Ej: Don't PUT OFF until tomorrow what you can do today. 

4. Lay off (Despedir por falta de trabajo): 
Ej: The factory had to LAY OFF 500 workers during the recession.
parts.audio: Welcome to Advanced Phrasal Verbs with Off and Out. Phrasal verbs with 'Off' often indicate separation, cancellation, or finishing something. Number 1: Call off, which means to cancel. For example: We had to CALL OFF the meeting due to the strike. Number 2: Write off, which means to accept that a debt will not be paid or an asset has lost its value. For example: The bank will WRITE OFF the bad loan. Number 3: Put off, which means to postpone. For example: Don't PUT OFF until tomorrow what you can do today. Number 4: Lay off, which means to dismiss staff because there is no work, not because of their performance. For example: The factory had to LAY OFF 500 workers during the recession.

parts.visual:
Los Phrasal Verbs con 'Out' suelen indicar expansión, finalización o descubrimiento: 

5. Roll out (Lanzar un producto / Implementar): 
Ej: Apple will ROLL OUT its new operating system next week. 

6. Phase out (Retirar gradualmente): 
Ej: We are going to PHASE OUT the old software over the next six months. 

7. Buy out (Comprar la parte de alguien / Adquirir): 
Ej: The larger company tried to BUY OUT our startup. 

8. Rule out (Descartar una posibilidad): 
Ej: We cannot RULE OUT the possibility of a hostile takeover.
parts.audio: Phrasal verbs with 'Out' often indicate expansion, completion, or discovery. Number 5: Roll out. To officially launch a new product or service. For example: Apple will ROLL OUT its new operating system next week. Number 6: Phase out. To gradually stop using or producing something. For example: We are going to PHASE OUT the old software over the next six months. Number 7: Buy out. To buy someone's share of a business, or acquire a whole company. For example: The larger company tried to BUY OUT our startup. Number 8: Rule out. To exclude or dismiss a possibility. For example: We cannot RULE OUT the possibility of a hostile takeover.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el Phrasal Verb corporativo correcto.

questions.question: Because the CEO is sick, we have to ____ off the press conference entirely. (Cancelar).
We are not canceling it, just delaying it. We need to ____ off the launch until next month. (Posponer).
During the pandemic, the airline had to ____ off 30% of its staff. (Despedir por causas económicas).
questions.explanation: Lay off = despedir personal (no por culpa del empleado, sino de la empresa).

questions.question: The debtor went bankrupt, so the bank had to ____ off the $10 million loan. (Dar por perdido).
questions.explanation: Write off = cancelar una deuda incobrable o deducir.

questions.question: Next quarter, the company plans to ____ out a massive new marketing campaign across Europe. (Lanzar/Implementar).
questions.explanation: Roll out = lanzar o implementar gradualmente un nuevo producto o servicio.

questions.question: We won't stop selling the old model immediately; we will ____ it out over the next year. (Retirar gradualmente).
questions.explanation: Phase out = retirar de circulación de forma gradual.

questions.question: To avoid a messy divorce, the founder decided to ____ out his partner's shares. (Comprar su parte).
questions.explanation: Buy out = comprar la participación de alguien para tomar el control.

questions.question: The police are investigating, but they cannot ____ out the possibility of corporate espionage. (Descartar).
questions.explanation: Rule out = descartar (una posibilidad, sospechoso, idea).

questions.question: The negotiations ____ down because neither side was willing to compromise. (Fracasaron/Se rompieron).
I need to ____ out how to fix this bug before the presentation. (Averiguar/Descubrir).
questions.explanation: Figure out = averiguar, entender cómo hacer algo resolviendo un problema.

questions.question: The meeting was dragging on, so the chairman tried to wrap it ____ quickly. (Concluir/Terminar).
questions.explanation: Wrap up = concluir, terminar una reunión o proyecto.

questions.question: They hired a consultant to iron ____ the remaining issues in the contract. (Solucionar detalles menores).
questions.explanation: Iron out = planchar, es decir, solucionar los últimos detalles o problemas menores.

questions.question: Our profits have leveled ____ after three years of rapid growth. (Estabilizarse tras subir).
questions.explanation: Level off = estabilizarse después de un periodo de subida o bajada.

questions.question: He was very tired, so he decided to sign ____ of his computer and go home. (Cerrar sesión).
questions.explanation: Sign off (o log off) = cerrar sesión o terminar una transmisión.

questions.question: The company was completely hollowed ____ by the private equity firm. (Vaciada).
questions.explanation: Hollow out = vaciar por dentro (quitar el valor o esencia de una empresa).

questions.question: The HR department needs to weed ____ the unqualified candidates from the pool. (Eliminar los malos/Filtrar).
questions.explanation: Weed out = arrancar la mala hierba (eliminar lo que no sirve de un grupo).

questions.question: Due to the scandal, the CEO was forced to step ____. (Renunciar a su cargo).
questions.explanation: Step down = renunciar a un alto cargo.

questions.question: I don't think we can pull ____ such a massive event with our small budget. (Lograr algo difícil).
questions.explanation: Pull off = lograr algo que parecía muy difícil o imposible.

questions.question: The new regulations were brought ____ last year. (Introducidas).
questions.explanation: Bring in = introducir o implementar (una ley o regla).

questions.question: Before we sign the contract, let me point ____ a few potential risks. (Señalar/Destacar).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la preposición correcta (off, out, up, down).

questions.question: Call ____ the meeting! (Cancelar)
Put it ____ until Friday. (Posponer)
Lay ____ 100 workers. (Despedir)
Write ____ the bad debt. (Dar por perdido)
Roll ____ the new software. (Lanzar)
Phase ____ the old machines. (Retirar gradualmente)
Buy ____ the competitor. (Comprar la parte)
Rule ____ the possibility. (Descartar)
Iron ____ the problems. (Solucionar detalles)
Wrap ____ the meeting. (Concluir/Terminar)
